svg.text: LINKEDIN — CLASS DESIGN (LLD)
THE FACADE + SEAM
LinkedIn — FACADE
service: LinkedInService (injected)
registerUser · updateProfile · sendConnectionRequest
acceptConnection · createPost · postJob · searchJobs · getFeed
«interface» LinkedInService
IDENTITY / PROFILE
registerUser · getUser · updateProfile(userId, User)
CONNECTIONS — mutual, consent-gated
sendConnectionRequest(sender, receiver, message)
acceptConnection(reqId, accepterId) · rejectConnection
getConnections · getPendingRequests
FOLLOW — asymmetric, no consent
follow / unfollow · getFollowers / getFollowing
CONTENT
createPost(authorId, content, PostType, PostVisibility)
getPost · likePost / unlikePost · commentOnPost · sharePost
getUserPosts · getFeed(userId, limit)
JOBS
postJob(companyId, title, description) · getJob
searchJobs(query, location) · closeJob(jobId)
SKILLS: addSkill · endorseSkill(userId, skillName, endorserId)
searchUsers(query) · every mutating call that needs consent carries the ACTOR id
THE CORE — four registries, no indexes
InMemoryLinkedInService
implements LinkedInService
users: ConcurrentHashMap<String, User>
posts: ConcurrentHashMap<String, Post>
jobs: ConcurrentHashMap<String, Job>
connectionRequests: ConcurrentHashMap<String, ConnectionRequest>
ids are UUIDs · no typed-id value objects · no secondary indexes at all
sendConnectionRequest — rejects self, duplicate pending, already-connected
requireRequestFor(reqId, responderId, action)
→ only the RECEIVER may accept or reject; anything else throws
acceptConnection — writes connectionIds on BOTH users
follow / unfollow — writes BOTH followingIds and followerIds
endorseSkill — rejects self-endorsement, resolves the named skill
getFeed — connections ∪ following ∪ PUBLIC, newest first, limit
searchJobs — ACTIVE only, then optional title and location contains
every lookup throws a typed exception — no silent nulls, no no-op mutations ✓
consent operations take the ACTOR id, so authorization is enforceable ✓
getFeed scans EVERY post — there is no posts-by-author index
searchJobs / searchUsers / getPendingRequests are O(n) toLowerCase scans
the duplicate-request check streams all requests AND is check-then-act
updateProfile REPLACES the whole User object — a lost-update race by design
registries are concurrent; the collections inside User and Post are NOT (except Skill)
THE MODEL — a profile is a document, a network is a graph
User — profile + three edge sets
userId (final) · name · email · headline · profilePicture
experiences: List<Experience> ← the PROFILE half
educations: List<Education> · skills: List<Skill>
connectionIds: Set<String> ← MUTUAL (1st degree)
followerIds / followingIds: Set<String> ← ASYMMETRIC
status: UserStatus · createdAt
addConnection / removeConnection · follow / unfollow
addFollower / removeFollower · addExperience / addSkill
every collection getter returns a defensive copy
this is what separates LinkedIn from a plain social graph: the profile ✓
the Lists / Sets here are plain ArrayList and HashSet — not concurrent
Skill — the one place done properly
name: String (final)
endorserIds: ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet()
endorse(endorserId): boolean
withdrawEndorsement(endorserId) · isEndorsedBy(id)
getEndorsements(): int ← derived from the SET SIZE
a SET of endorser ids, not an int counter — so:
• re-endorsing is a no-op, not a +1 (idempotent by construction)
• withdrawing is exact — a counter could not be decremented safely
• "who endorsed me?" is answerable, which the product needs
the same idea as Post.likeUserIds — identity, not arithmetic ✓
Post
postId · authorId (final) · content · mediaUrls
type: PostType (STATUS_UPDATE / ARTICLE / JOB_SHARE / ...)
visibility: PostVisibility (PUBLIC / CONNECTIONS / ...)
likeUserIds: Set<String> · comments: List<Comment> · shares: int
likeUserIds is a Set ⇒ double-liking is a no-op ✓
sharePost copies the TEXT ("Shared: ..."), it does not reference
the original — so an edit never propagates, and attribution is lost
Job · Experience · Education
Job: jobId, companyId (final), title, description, location,
JobType, salaryRange, requiredSkills, JobStatus, postedAt
closeJob flips status to CLOSED; searchJobs filters ACTIVE first
no JobApplication entity — applying is out of scope here
Experience: title, company, dates, current: boolean
Education: school, degree, fieldOfStudy, dates, grade
plain mutable structs — they are profile data, not domain logic
ConnectionRequest — the consent handshake
requestId · senderId · receiverId (all final) · message · createdAt
status: RequestStatus · accept() · reject()
PENDING
accept(reqId, accepterId)
reject(reqId, rejecterId)
ACCEPTED
REJECTED
ACCEPTED writes connectionIds on BOTH users — mutual by construction ✓
honest: accept() / reject() do NOT guard the current status, so a re-accept silently re-fires
TWO EDGE KINDS — the distinction the graph turns on
CONNECTION (1st degree) — mutual, needs an accept, symmetric
one edge stored as two set entries: sender.connectionIds and receiver.connectionIds
FOLLOW — one-sided, no consent, still two set entries
follower.followingIds AND followee.followerIds — kept in sync by hand
THE BUG THIS SHAPE INVITES: follow() wrote both sides, unfollow() cleared only one.
The followee listed a stale follower forever and follower counts drifted upward permanently.
Fix: unfollow() must mirror follow() exactly — write both sides, or neither ✓
a real store makes this ONE edge row; two denormalized sets is the price of in-memory O(1) reads
WHAT MAKES THIS "LINKEDIN" AND NOT "FACEBOOK"
1. The profile is a first-class document — Experience, Education, Skill.
a social network has a bio; a professional network has a resume
2. Endorsement is a social signal on a profile field — modelled as a set of
endorser ids so it is idempotent, withdrawable and attributable.
3. Jobs are a second content type with their own lifecycle (ACTIVE / CLOSED)
and their own search — title + location, ACTIVE-only.
4. Connections are consent-gated, and degree-of-separation is the ranking
signal — though 2nd/3rd degree is NOT computed here, only 1st.
WHITEBOARD ORDER:
① LinkedIn facade → LinkedInService seam → ② the four registries → ③ User = profile + three edge sets → ④ ConnectionRequest's handshake → ⑤ Skill's endorser set → Job search
LEGEND

g.text: Patterns: Facade · service seam (DI) · graph modelled as denormalized edge sets · set-backed counters (endorsements, likes) · consent handshake
NOT present, and worth saying so: no Strategy for feed ranking, no Observer for notifications, no typed ids, no 2nd-degree computation
Honest gaps: no secondary indexes (every search and the feed are O(n) scans) · updateProfile replaces the whole User · model collections not concurrent
